doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Spirituality, personal transgressions and life as a movie
summary: Says his own actions, not his spirituality, caused suffering; life is a movie, and the body is made to last.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Has there been times in your life when you have felt your own spirituality has suffered and your life has suffered because of it? And then you changed?

No I don’t think that my life has ever suffered because of my spirituality. What I think has happened is that I have transgressed my own spiritual beliefs. I have lied. I have committed adultery. I have ingested drugs of various kinds. These are crimes against your spirit. And I have committed such crimes. And so my spirituality hasn’t been the cause of any illness or wrongfulness. My own actions have done that, as it does with everyone. Every act you commit you pay for. It’s like a movie theater. When I was a kid I couldn’t get in that movie until I paid a dime. I had to pay the dime to get in. It’s the same in this life. We’re all in a movie.

I always say, people say, “you look great for 78” you know. “How do you feel?” I say I feel just like I feel when I went to the movies. I’m not leaving until this movie ends. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -4-
Man I hope it’s a double feature for you.

But I think that’s the way life is you know. If you’re interested in life and you’re into life, you’ll live forever. Because I think, as the ancient Greek philosopher said, “we do not die, we kill ourselves.” Man as a creative being, if you examine him, he’s made to last eternally. There’s no malfunctioning in the original construction of the human anatomy. The body is made to last forever. We kill it with what we do. And so I try to do as little to my body of an inimical nature, as I possibly can, and I’m still working on that. Because I like sugar and sugar is poison. I like ice cream — too much milk is bad for the system. I’m always running up against it. How come it tastes so good? I’m still about six years old when it comes to that. You know all this talk of knowledge, when it comes to what you really want you’re an ignoramus.
Well you have to have a few challenges to build your character you know — for something to work on.
I suppose. Well I know that’s true. That’s true.
